name: bash
plain: `bash` is the program that reads what you type in the terminal and runs it. It also runs scripts: text files full of commands with variables, tests and loops.

Much of CTF work is bash: chaining tools with pipes, looping over files or ports, and writing quick one-liners. This page is focused on the habits and syntax you use most, not every option of the very large bash manual.
when: Chain commands with pipes and redirects.
Loop over a list of hosts, files or numbers.

examples.title: Run a command and use its output
examples.explain: $(...) runs a command and pastes its output in place (command substitution).

examples.title: Variables
examples.explain: No spaces around =. Use $name to read it, and quote it so spaces do not break things.

examples.title: Pipes and redirects
examples.cmd:
cat access.log | grep 404 | wc -l
ls > files.txt
ls >> files.txt
cmd 2> errors.txt
cmd > all.txt 2>&1
examples.explain: | feeds one command into the next; > overwrites; >> appends; 2> redirects errors; 2>&1 sends errors to the same place as output.

examples.title: Loop over a list
examples.cmd: for ip in 10.10.10.{1..5}; do ping -c1 -W1 $ip >/dev/null && echo "$ip up"; done
examples.explain: {1..5} expands to five addresses. && runs the echo only if ping succeeded.

examples.title: Read a file line by line
examples.cmd: while read -r line; do echo "[$line]"; done < users.txt
examples.explain: The loop runs once per line. -r keeps backslashes as they are.

examples.title: A test and a branch
examples.cmd: if [ -f flag.txt ]; then cat flag.txt; else echo 'no flag'; fi
examples.explain: [ ] is the test command; see man test for all the checks.

examples.title: A small script
examples.explain: Save as check.sh, run chmod +x check.sh, then ./check.sh a b c. set -euo pipefail makes the script stop on errors and unset variables.

examples.title: Run a string as bash
examples.explain: -c runs the string instead of a file; the words after it become $0, $1... Useful in xargs and cron.

examples.title: History tricks
examples.explain: !! repeats the last command; sudo !! repeats it with sudo; !$ is its last word; Ctrl+R searches your history as you type.

examples.title: Keyboard shortcuts
examples.cmd: Ctrl+A / Ctrl+E / Ctrl+W / Ctrl+U / Ctrl+L / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+D
examples.explain: Start of line, end of line, delete word, delete to start, clear screen, interrupt, end of input (exit).

examples.title: Brace and glob expansion
examples.explain: The shell expands braces and wildcards before the command sees them: file.{txt,bak} becomes file.txt file.bak.

mistakes: Spaces around = in an assignment (a = 1 runs a command named a).
Not quoting variables: a file called 'my file' becomes two arguments.
Using [ $x = y ] when $x is empty or has spaces.
Parsing ls output: use globs or find instead.
Forgetting set -euo pipefail in scripts and missing failures.
Writing scripts with Windows (CRLF) line endings: bash says ^M: bad interpreter.
Running untrusted one-liners (curl | bash) without reading them.
